description: Spaghetti alla Carbonara Classic is a timeless Roman pasta dish, celebrated for its rich, creamy sauce made from egg yolks, Pecorino Romano cheese, guanciale, and black pepper. This iconic recipe delivers a perfect balance of savory, peppery, and cheesy flavors, coating each strand of spaghetti in pure Italian indulgence. It is a true testament to simple ingredients creating extraordinary taste.

instructions.title: Prepare the Guanciale
instructions.text: Dice the guanciale into small strips or cubes. Place it in a cold large skillet or pan over medium-low heat. Cook slowly until the fat has rendered and the guanciale is crispy and golden. Remove the crispy guanciale with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving the rendered fat in the pan. Keep the pan off the heat for now.

instructions.title: Cook the Spaghetti
instructions.text: Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a rolling boil. Add the spaghetti and cook according to package instructions until al dente. Before draining, reserve about 1 to 1.5 cups of the starchy pasta water. This water is crucial for creating the creamy sauce.

instructions.title: Prepare the Egg and Cheese Mixture
instructions.text: While the pasta cooks, in a medium bowl, whisk together the egg yolks, the whole egg, and the finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese. Add a generous amount of freshly ground black pepper. Whisk until the mixture is smooth and well combined. This is your carbonara sauce base.

instructions.title: Combine Pasta and Sauce
instructions.text: Once the spaghetti is al dente, drain it quickly but do not rinse. Immediately transfer the hot spaghetti directly into the pan with the rendered guanciale fat (make sure the pan is no longer on direct heat to prevent the eggs from scrambling). Toss the pasta to coat it evenly with the fat.

instructions.title: Emulsify the Carbonara
instructions.text: Pour the egg and cheese mixture over the hot spaghetti in the pan. Immediately add a ladleful (about 1/4 cup) of the reserved hot pasta water. Toss vigorously and continuously with tongs, lifting the pasta to coat every strand. The heat from the pasta and the pan, combined with the pasta water, will gently cook the eggs and create a rich, creamy emulsion. Add more pasta water, a tablespoon at a time, if needed, to achieve the desired creamy consistency. Do not overheat, as this will scramble the eggs.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Stir in most of the crispy guanciale, reserving some for garnish. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary, though the Pecorino Romano and guanciale are usually salty enough. Serve immediately in warm bowls, topped with the reserved crispy guanciale, extra grated Pecorino Romano, and a final generous grinding of fresh black pepper. Buon appetito!

tips: Always use guanciale for authentic Carbonara; its unique fat and flavor are irreplaceable. If unavailable, use pancetta, but guanciale is truly superior.

The key to a creamy sauce without scrambling the eggs is to remove the pan from the heat before adding the egg mixture. The residual heat from the pasta and pan, combined with hot pasta water, will create the perfect emulsion.
Serve immediately! Carbonara is best enjoyed fresh off the stove. The sauce can thicken quickly as it cools, so prepare your bowls and serve without delay.
